summary: Tottenham lost 2-1 at home to West Ham on 7 December 2023 despite leading early through Cristian Romero, suffering their fourth defeat in five and conceding two goals from poor defending. Captain Heung-Min Son called the performance unacceptable, while Ange Postecoglou and Tim Sherwood criticised finishing and game management. In the other match Everton beat Newcastle 3-0 despite a ten point penalty.
one_line: Spurs lost 2-1 to West Ham after leading 1-0, with two awful goals conceded, while Everton beat Newcastle 3-0.
key_facts: Tottenham lost 2-1 at home to West Ham, their fourth defeat in five matches.
Cristian Romero put Spurs 1-0 up with an early header.
Jarrod Bowen levelled after a Mohammed Kudus shot deflected off two Spurs players.
James Ward-Prowse scored the winner on the rebound after hitting the post, following Destiny Udogie's blind backpass.
Captain Heung-Min Son said "this is unacceptable" and that Spurs were "soft".
Ange Postecoglou said both goals conceded were terrible and the team's finishing was poor.
Tim Sherwood said on Optus Sport that Spurs are five games without a win and leave space when they lead.
OptaJoe said Tottenham are the first Premier League side to fail to win five consecutive games despite going 1-0 up in each, and to lose three consecutive home games after going 1-0 up in each.
Spurs had drawn 3-3 at Manchester City the weekend before, but are now fifth, level with Manchester United and outside the Champions League spots.
West Ham moved up to ninth, three points behind Spurs; David Moyes said "we just about scraped it".
Everton beat Newcastle 3-0 with goals from Dwight McNeil, Abdoulaye Doucoure and Beto, moving clear of the relegation zone despite a ten point penalty for financial irregularities.
Sean Dyche said Everton would have 20 points without the penalty and spoke of an appeal.
Newcastle manager Eddie Howe said "We have to do better", citing injuries; they had lost to Everton and Bournemouth after beating Manchester United, Arsenal and Chelsea.
